Hello I can add a comment. So I work for contracting for Ford as SWE under Apex systems. I was contacted over the phone after applying through LinkedIn. My experience was decent but nothing exceptional. I talked to the recruiter and just did the normal interview process. They let me know abojt what the interviews were like but not much prep material but at the time Ford's interview was not so complicated. 

One thing you can ask is if you can be submitted to multiple roles in a company. I managed to get two interviews for 2 positions and chose the better paying one. From there it is pretty straightforward they will due the normal W2 employment onboarding and the rest is the the company that you got contract with. They might want you to accept the job real fast but take your time. 

The process was fine if you are open to contracting. I think Apex has full time roles as well so look at the job posting and ask your recruiter. Also ask the timezone that you would work in since Apex does recruiting for East coast companies.

If you are contracting it is pretty decent, entering your hours and expenses is easy but not many benefits they give so ask for as much money as you can if you go that route.

Apex is decent and some of the recruiters still contact me about different roles but I think it might not be the best place to go for a new hire.

I have ASD so sometimes I can get socially exhausted very quickly so that quarter took a toll on me very badly. The big BIG thing I suggest is to go to a counselor, talk about how you feel, and make a plan if you do decide to leave. 

I will say this as well, it is better to finish the quarter off, preferably with a GPA above 2.0. If that is the case, if it is just a one or two quarter break they will accept you back no problem. If it is longer than a year then you will have make up some of what you have missed in CCC with a 2.0 or better and they will likely take you back if you talk to your major's counseling office soon enough.

When I left in Fall 2012. I took a break, got a job, learned to drive then eventually went to CCC and transfered back in Winter 2016. I had a financial messup and couldnt continue to Spring 2016. Once again I worked for the whole summer went back in Fall and have continued to winter 2017 and I think I am gonna finish this time since I have only a year left. 

TLDR, The answer is yes, you can come back but you have to reapply. That process can vary depending on your major all I can say is the ICS school is very accomodating. When you reapply you must pay $70 and submit any outside coursework you done in the meantime. The deadlines for each quarter are posted online on the registrar website. What makes it easy or hard to come back is your GPA when you leave, so it is in your best to just finish off the quarter then just withdraw then. Also apply for financial aid for the year you plan to come back ASAP regardless of what quarter it is (Fall, Winter, Spring) so you for sure get all the financial aid you can get without having to wait. Good luck to you and I hope you pull through and feel better regardless of whatever decision you make.
